subject: Velora Health: tailored log retention & minimization playbook
messages:
From: Lucy Tan <lucy.tan@velorahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@velorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2029 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: scoped log retention & minimization approach for PHI-handling tenants

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Velora's InfoSec team is compiling a scoped retention and minimization plan for our integration with Redwood's Private deployment. Two asks for you: 1) a mapping of what session/trace logs (and retention windows) you retain at the tenant level, and 2) an outline of options for targeted retention carveouts for tenants that process PHI (we need to show compensating controls to our auditors).

Our timeline is tight — can you provide a high-level playbook and any sample artifacts we can show auditors by EOD Thursday? If you need a formal SIG/CUSTOM questionnaire, we can send one, but an engineering-playbook + matrix will do for now.

Appreciate it — Lucy

Lucy Tan
Director, Information Security
Velora Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lucy Tan <lucy.tan@velorahealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped log retention & minimization approach for PHI-handling tenants

Lucy —

Appreciate the clear asks. We'll put together a short playbook and a tenant-level retention matrix that shows default retention, ephemeral traces, and options for carveouts (e.g., 0-day debug traces, 30/90/365d tiers, secure escrow). I'm looping in Neha (security/compliance) and Markus (runtime engineering) to confirm what evidence artifacts we can include (SIG/CAIQ pointers, sampling scripts, proof-of-delete notes).

We're aiming to deliver a draft pack by Thu EOD. Quick Q: do your auditors require chain-of-custody artifacts for deleted data, or is a signed attestation + API logs sufficient?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velora request - evidence and playbook contents

Marissa / Markus —

From a SOC2/SIG perspective, auditors usually accept: (a) a retention matrix mapping data class -> default TTL, (b) a scoped exception policy describing customer-requested carveouts, (c) proof-of-delete artifacts (API call IDs + timestamps), and (d) sampling evidence showing deletion executed across a subset of tenant IDs. Chain-of-custody is helpful for legal holds but not always required for routine retention changes.

I'll prepare a checklist of artifacts we can deliver quickly: CAIQ excerpts, SIG control IDs for retention, sample CLI/API delete logs (redacted), and a brief attestation template for Velora to sign. Markus — can you confirm whether the runtime can produce per-tenant deletion receipts (uuid + timestamp) and an export of retention settings?

-Neha
Senior Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Velora request - runtime capabilities

Neha / Marissa —

Yes: runtime can emit per-tenant deletion receipts. Format is simple JSON lines (delete_id, tenant_id, object_type, deleted_at, operator_id). We can also produce a sampled export (CSV) for a chosen tenant list that shows when each retention bucket was enforced. For Velora's PHI tenants we recommend:

- Default: 30 days token & session traces
- For PHI flagged tenants: 0-day session trace retention (only ephemeral in memory, no persistent session logs), with KV-cache automatic purge after 1 hour and an optional escrow snapshot for forensics (encrypted, customer-controlled KMS).
- Audit evidence: delete receipts + sampling export + CAIQ/SIG mapping docs.

I'll assemble the CSV template and a short FAQ line for auditors. ETA Thu AM for a draft.

-Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lucy Tan <lucy.tan@velorahealth.com>, security@velorahealth.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 14:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped log retention & minimization approach for PHI-handling tenants

Lucy —

Attached is a draft playbook and a tenant retention matrix that addresses your two asks: mapping of retained artifacts and a recommended segmentation approach for PHI tenants. Highlights:

- Playbook summary (one page): defaults, exception process, and auditing evidence we can provide.
- Retention matrix (CSV attached): per-artifact TTLs, whether retained by tenant or platform, and evidence type (delete_receipt, sample_export, CAIQ ref).
- Recommended PHI configuration: 0-day persistent session retention + 1h KV-cache expiry + optional encrypted escrow.
- Evidence pack we can deliver: (1) CAIQ control excerpts, (2) 50-sample delete_receipts for one Velora PHI tenant, (3) a short signed attestation template for procurement.

Attachments: velora-retention-matrix-2029-04-11.csv, proposed-segmentation-playbook.pdf

We can run the sample export for one tenant this week if you confirm the tenant IDs. If auditors need chain-of-custody instead of attestation, let us know and we'll escalate operationally.

Next steps: please confirm the tenant list (or provide a test tenant) and whether procurement needs a formal SIG questionnaire. We'll hand off the attestation once you confirm wording.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Marissa.Coale@redwood.com
Phone: (415) 555-0198
